Concept: Attachment to national or provincial culture
Rule: Our / demonym / Western / nation or province possessive (’s or 's) within 5 words before a culture term (identity, character, culture, way of life, tradition, heritage, pride, values, customs, legacy, achievement…). Vetoes: arts, film, TV, museums, grants, funding, culture sector, heritage fund, First Nations, Indigenous, Aboriginal, Métis, Inuit, democratic, institution, Chinese; immigrants, diversity or multiculturalism only alongside enrich, welcome, celebrate or contribute
foreign + a threat, interference or control term (interests, attacks, owned, funded, interference, ban, corporations, speculators, meddling, horrible…) (same sentence)

Concept: Hostility to the nation or province
Rule: Phrase: anti- + Canada, a province, a demonym or Western (anti-Canadian, anti-Alberta, anti-Quebec…)
Phrase: homeland, native land, home and native land

Defensive verb (preserve, protect, defend, safeguard, conserve, maintain, uphold) within 5 words of our / demonym / province, then within 5 words of a culture term (heritage, culture, identity, way of life, tradition, values); or a culture term within 5 words of of (the) + our / demonym / province, with no defensive verb

Concept: Attachment to or defence of tradition

Vetoes: First Nations, Indigenous, Aboriginal, Métis, Inuit, native…; traditional (+1 word) industries / companies / measures

Concept: Authentic or deserving members of the nation

Enemy term (enemy, destroyer, traitor, betrayer) + Canada, a province, a demonym or Western (Canada) (same sentence); of / ’s optional
